label: GO-step detector (fires on every GO step)
explanation: Fires on 100% of GO steps (all trials, all rel positions) and essentially never at D1 or D2 (1164 tiny D1 activations, ~0% of mass, mostly when the previous trial was unrewarded or a penalty). phase == GO gives dev precision 1.00, recall 0.997, F1 0.998. Activation is near-constant (median 6.8, max 7.6), so this is mostly a phase/position feature; any extra information sits in its magnitude. Checked magnitude effects: it is higher when the upcoming choice is a1 (a1 GO steps make up 97% of the top activation quartile and 13% of the bottom one) and higher after a rewarded previous trial (prev_reward==1: 88% of the top quartile vs 30% of the bottom). It does not depend on policy confidence |choice|, transition type, or the hidden good state.

issues: Test split: phase == GO scores precision 1.000, recall 0.996, F1 0.998, mass recall 0.9998, with no false positives. Coverage is 0.985 in the lowest activation quartile and 1.0 in the others.

There are 1479 test misses, all at D1, with tiny activations (about 0.01-0.08 of max) and about 0% of the mass. They are spread over every rel position. (D1, in_rew==0) has precision 0.008 and (D1, in_rew==1) has precision 0.001, so 'mostly after an unrewarded trial' is directionally right (about 80% of D1 firings follow in_rew 0), but the class is too weak to count as systematic.
Minor: the in_rew == -1 rows that fire at 94.5% in the profile are GO-phase steps. (D1, in_rew==-1) has almost no firings, so the 'penalty trial' part of the D1 claim is not supported.

I could not verify the magnitude claims (a1 above a2, prev_reward==1 higher) directly, because the score tool is binary. The miss windows agree with them: a1 GO steps are about 0.87-0.97 of max and a2 about 0.79-0.86. These claims are secondary to the label in any case.
